metdefs.q: "Percent of time over the past sample period during which one or more kernels was executing on the GPU." (nvidia-smi documentation, the same reading)
metdefs.how: share of slices with any kernel running, weighted by the share of the slice it ran

metdefs.q: "The fraction of time at least one warp was active on a multiprocessor, averaged over all multiprocessors. Note that “active” does not necessarily mean a warp is actively computing. For instance, warps waiting on memory requests are considered active."
metdefs.how: mean over slices and over the 132 SMs of (SM has a resident warp)

metdefs.q: "The fraction of resident warps on a multiprocessor, relative to the maximum number of concurrent warps supported on a multiprocessor ... Higher occupancy does not necessarily indicate better GPU usage."
metdefs.how: mean over slices and SMs of resident warps / 64

metdefs.q: "The fraction of cycles the tensor (HMMA / IMMA) pipe was active ... An activity of 0.2 (20%) could indicate 20% of the SMs are at 100% utilization over the entire time period, 100% of the SMs are at 20% utilization ... or any combination in between."
metdefs.how: mean over slices and SMs of the tensor-pipe share of cycles

metdefs.q: "The fraction of cycles where data was sent to or received from device memory ... (in practice a peak of ~0.8 (80%) is the maximum achievable)."
metdefs.how: mean over slices of the memory-interface share

metdefs.q: "The rate of data transmitted / received over NVLink, not including protocol headers, in bytes per second." (dcgm_fields.h says "including both header and payload": the two sources disagree)
metdefs.how: shown here as a share of link bandwidth
